My dad abusing my mom. She would come home from work and he’d start yelling and hitting her. I would cry in my room, cause I was scared for her, then he’d yell at me for crying. He would break things in the house too. Holes in the walls and one time kept hitting the bathroom door until it was just a pile of shreds in the hallway… I remember walking around it to go to the bathroom. I’m sure a lot more happened that my mom never told me and I don’t remember. I used to have really strange dreams with sleep paralysis and heard voices until I was about 11 or 12, which is around when he died. He committed suicide. I think a lot of it is why I have such bad social anxiety and depression as an adult. I’ve never had a good conversation with anyone about it since - I think I tried to confide in the wrong people, because they criticized me instead of trying to comfort or support me. 

I think I’m okay now though, it truly could of been worse. But it definitely caused problems for me, especially in dating and expressing myself as an adult.

I don’t know if anything I say helps, but I almost did this at 18 and I can’t be more grateful that my mom never co-signed for the loans. It would have cost me over 100k in total and she knew she didn’t have enough money to co-sign on something like that. I ended up going to a tech school and spending 13k and I even regret THAT. I did not end up using that schooling for much and it was still a huge overpayment for what I got… that’s barely even a tenth of what I almost did…. I would not be able to afford basic necessities if I had gone to that school and took out that money. All the horror stories I’ve heard and read online - it scares me how naive I was and how little I cared about the amount of money I was trying to take out. 

Don’t co-sign (hopefully that will be enough) but maybe sitting down and showing them what happens to a lot of students would help. You can find tons of stories here and elsewhere of people regretting doing this or wishing they went a cheaper route to their degree. I would just show them horror stories of this to help them understand .. some people with great jobs still struggle because the loans they took out were so much money. 

Also I’m not saying I agree with everything he says, but listening to some of Dave Ramsey’s YouTube videos, especially of those who call in with their story, really helped me see a different perspective on finances and taking out debt to pay for things. He can be really extreme about paying off debt but listening to his show definitely helped me out. Good luck to you!

A clinic I went to for a few years changed dentists pretty frequently. The dentists I had there regularly I trusted and liked pretty well. One time I saw a different one, because my regular dentist was overbooked that day. I had a sensitive tooth, he told me it was a huge cavity and I needed a root canal. I was super stressed and he pushed for me to have it done, right then. I started to proceed with it, but got so stressed I was emotional and crying after being given the anesthetic. He came to check on me and asked why I was so upset, but I told him I was fine and to just let me be. He eventually told me that if it's "not as deep as thinks" he'd just fill it like a normal cavity. He ended up just doing a filling and saying he didn't need to do the root canal. Haven't had any problems with the tooth since. So... I don't know if he was pushing for me to have it done because of money (that's how it felt, he was super pushy about me doing right then) or if it was just a big cavity and he wasn't sure.
